technical.lead: FMRB EO Monday witness slate adds CISA Director; ACLU + CDT join amicus
technical.body: The Frontier Model Review Board executive-order interagency-review track opens Monday with a sharpened May 15 14:00 EDT S-407 classified threshold briefing witness slate. Senator Mark Warner's office confirms the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Director joining the previously-confirmed NIST Director Locascio, ODNI cyber lead, NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director, and Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center representative as the fifth witness, focusing the operational view on federal-civilian-executive-branch agentic-AI deployment exposure. The American Civil Liberties Union and the Center for Democracy and Technology file a joint Monday amicus letter joining the AI Policy Institute, R Street, Public Knowledge, Lawyers for Civil Justice, Knight First Amendment Institute, and Electronic Frontier Foundation coalition pressing the documented State Farm reasoned-decision-record argument plus a 60-day Defense Production Act Section 708 public-comment window. White House OSTP holds its line that the draft remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22, leaving CISA as the operative federal-civilian enforcement vehicle as the May 21 n8n federal-civilian remediation deadline lands first.

technical.lead: Indo-Pacific cyber-eval reciprocity perimeter widens to ten jurisdictions
technical.body: The Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter reaches its first ten-jurisdiction Monday count. Indonesia's National Cyber and Crypto Agency plus the Ministry of Communication and Informatics jointly publish a Monday entry note signaling intent to enter the Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI memorandum-of-cooperation cohort as a formal observer with a 150-day domestic-consultation window targeting Q4 2026 mirror signature; Vietnam's Ministry of Information and Communications separately confirms observer entry under Track II shoulder-to-shoulder arrangements parallel to the Taiwan NICS Sunday announcement. The cohort now spans ten named candidates (Singapore, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand formally; Canada, Australia, India, Taiwan, Indonesia, Vietnam as observers) plus the originating UK and EU. Mistral, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind reaffirm cohort participation; the operational threshold remains Mythos-class capability plus GPT-5.5-class capability. The United States recognition gap is now a full Monday wider than the Friday baseline.

technical.lead: LangChain LangGraph CVE-2026-44712 completes seven-CVE agent-loader wave
technical.body: A fresh agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE drops Monday-morning Pacific time, completing the agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader exposure pattern coverage. LangChain CVE-2026-44712 (CVSS 8.7) is a checkpoint deserialization vulnerability in the LangGraph agent-state-replay path matching the AutoGen CVE-2026-44612 pattern disclosed Sunday; LangChain ships LangGraph v0.7.2 same-day with the patch plus a backport advisory for the v0.5.x and v0.6.x branches the NHS England blocklist references. Trail of Bits publishes a Monday extended write-up taxonomizing the seven agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs that have landed across the May 5-11 wave (CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, LangChain, plus the Friday LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 and LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188), proposing a common-mitigation pattern signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist-validation enforced at the framework boundary. DeepMind, Meta AI, and Anthropic co-publish a Monday joint preprint (arxiv 2605.06342) proposing a common signed-checkpoint format and manifest-allowlist-validation schema with reference implementations in Python and Rust; Microsoft, LangChain, and the CrewAI maintainer team publish parallel Monday commitments to ship as default in the next minor-version release with a coordinated mid-June target window.

technical.lead: Cerebras opens second week +9.5% as Tenstorrent files S-1 cover note
technical.body: Cerebras CBRS opens its second trading week with a clean Monday gap-up. The opening print at $189.40 lifts the stock 9.5 percent from the Friday close of $172.85, validating Sunday's buyside-note season target raises (Morgan Stanley to $192, Jefferies initiation at $178, Goldman holding $185 with $220 upside scenario) without testing the Bernstein $172 Market-Perform floor. Tenstorrent files its confidential S-1 final pre-submission cover note on Monday with the SEC filing window opening today per the JOBS Act EGC framework; the submission cover note discloses joint lead bookrunners J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, and Citi plus Asia-Pacific co-managers Mizuho Securities and SMBC Nikko reflecting Hyundai Motor Group and Samsung Foundry co-anchor positions. Jim Keller publishes a Monday investor-relations note ratifying the early-August public-filing window pending the standard SEC 30-60 day review. SambaNova Systems separately publishes a Monday market-conditions update confirming Wells Fargo Securities as joint lead with the late-June confidential-submission target unchanged.

technical.lead: Unsloth Monday tensor-parallel router-attention adds dual-Hopper INT4 export
technical.body: Unsloth ships its Monday changelog adding a fourth refinement track to the multi-GPU NCCL backend for the router-only LoRA recipe. The update brings a tensor-parallel mode for the router-attention forward pass on dual-Hopper workstation tiers (H100 SXM5 plus H100 PCIe combinations) reporting a further 17 percent peak combined VRAM reduction versus the Sunday NCCL-only multi-GPU mode plus a 28 percent forward-pass latency improvement on Llama 4 Behemoth router-only inference, an extended ONNX export path supporting INT4 quantization for the router-only adapters targeting the Meta Llama 4 plus Mistral Codestral plus Kimi K2.6 deployment cohort, plus a community-contributed recipe for the new Qwen3-Next 480B-A40B Mixture-of-Experts model showing 9 percent peak combined VRAM versus the dense baseline on a quad-RTX 6000 Ada workstation. A second Hacker News reproduction lands within hours documenting the dual-H100 PCIe workstation completing the Mixtral 8x22B router-only recipe at 11 percent peak combined VRAM, consolidating the commodity-and-prosumer-hardware accessibility narrative. The Stable Long-Context Reinforcement Learning via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition (arxiv 2605.05844 v4) Monday extension shows the technique closes the long-context training-stability gap on the new dual-H100 PCIe tensor-parallel setup, with pre-tested integration against vLLM v0.11.2 tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode.
